question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Beat around the bush
option_1: To avoid talking about what is important
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. To avoid talking about what is important.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "beat around the bush" means to avoid coming to the main point; to talk about unimportant things instead of saying what one really means. (मुद्दे की बात न करके इधर-उधर की बातें करना)

◦ Example: Stop beating around the bush and tell me how much the repair will cost.

• The expression comes from hunting, where beaters would strike the bushes around the game instead of going straight for the bird itself.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "To talk about important things" is the exact opposite of the idiom's meaning.

• Option 3 "To have patience" and Option 4 "To avoid people" have no connection with the idiom; the idiom is about avoiding a topic, not people.

NOTE

• Related idioms: "come to the point" / "cut to the chase" (to get straight to the main issue — the antonyms of this idiom), "mince words" (to soften what one says), "hem and haw" (to hesitate while speaking).

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

A person who is kept captive for fulfilment of demands of money or conditions.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Hostage.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "hostage" is a person who is seized and held captive by someone so that certain demands (money, ransom, release of prisoners, political conditions) are met. (बंधक)

◦ Example: The hijackers held forty passengers hostage for three days.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Doyen" — the most respected or senior member of a group or profession. (मुखिया / वरिष्ठतम व्यक्ति)

• Option 2 "Bait" — food or an object used to attract and trap an animal or person; it is not a captive human being.

• Option 4 "Scion" — a descendant or young member of a famous or wealthy family. (वंशज)

NOTE

• Related one-word substitutes: captive (one held prisoner), abductor/kidnapper (one who carries a person away unlawfully), ransom (money demanded for a hostage's release), detainee (a person held in custody).

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Peril
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Danger.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Peril" (noun) means serious and immediate danger; grave risk. Its closest synonym is therefore "danger". (गंभीर खतरा / जोखिम)

◦ Example: The sailors were in great peril during the storm.

• As an adjective it becomes "perilous" (extremely dangerous) — e.g., a perilous journey across the mountains.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Entertainment" (amusement) and Option 3 "Joke" (something said to cause laughter) are unrelated and carry a positive/light sense.

• Option 4 "Ignorance" (lack of knowledge) refers to the mind, not to risk.

NOTE

• Synonyms of peril: danger, hazard, jeopardy, risk, menace, threat. Antonyms: safety, security, protection. Useful phrase: "at one's own peril" (at one's own risk).

question:
There is a spelling error in the given sentence. Select the option that contains the INCORRECTLY spelt word.

As per manager’s opinion, the laser sprinkler malfuntioned.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. malfuntioned.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Malfuntioned" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "malfunctioned" — it needs a "c" before the "t" (mal + function + ed). It means failed to work properly / worked in a faulty way. (ठीक से काम न करना)

◦ Correct: As per manager's opinion, the laser sprinkler malfunctioned.

• Spelling key: MAL + FUNC + TION + ED.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "sprinkler" (a device that sprays water in drops), "laser" (a device producing an intense narrow beam of light) and "opinion" (a view or judgement) are all spelt correctly.

NOTE

• The prefix "mal-" means bad/wrong: malfunction, malpractice, malnutrition, maladjusted, maltreatment. "LASER" is an acronym — Light Amplification by Stimulated Emission of Radiation.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Amiable
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Unfriendly.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Amiable" means friendly, pleasant, good-natured and easy to like. Its direct antonym is "unfriendly" (not kind or pleasant towards others). (मिलनसार का विलोम — अमित्रवत / रूखा)

◦ Example: The amiable host made every guest feel welcome, whereas the unfriendly manager barely nodded.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Restless" (unable to stay still) refers to physical/mental agitation, not to friendliness.

• Option 3 "Sad" (unhappy) and Option 4 "Joyful" (very happy) describe mood, whereas amiable describes temperament towards others. Option 4 is closer to a synonym in tone, not an antonym.

NOTE

• Synonyms of amiable: affable, cordial, genial, congenial, good-humoured, sociable. Antonyms: unfriendly, hostile, surly, aloof, disagreeable. Do not confuse amiable (of people) with amicable (of relations/settlements — friendly, without quarrelling).

question:
Select the most appropriate idiom to fill in the blank.

Rahul speaks easily in front of a small group, but he seems ________ before a large audience.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. ill at ease.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "ill at ease" means uncomfortable, uneasy, nervous or awkward in a situation. The contrast word "but" shows that Rahul, who is comfortable with a small group, becomes uneasy before a large audience. (असहज / बेचैन)

◦ Correct: Rahul speaks easily in front of a small group, but he seems ill at ease before a large audience.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "think ill of" means to have a poor opinion of someone — it needs an object (think ill of him) and does not fit after "seems".

• Option 3 "man of ill repute" means a person with a bad reputation — a noun phrase, not a state of nervousness.

• Option 4 "ill-disposed to" means unwilling or hostile towards — it expresses unwillingness, not nervousness.

NOTE

• Grammar clue: after the linking verb "seems" we need an adjectival phrase describing a state; only "ill at ease" fits. Opposite idiom: "at ease" (relaxed and comfortable).

question:
Select the most appropriate idiom for the following sentence.

He made the business profitable from unprofitable in about a year of joining.
option_3: Where there is a will, there is a way
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Where there is a will, there is a way.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The proverb "Where there is a will, there is a way" means if a person is truly determined to do something, he/she will find a method of doing it however difficult it may be. (जहाँ चाह, वहाँ राह)

◦ The sentence describes a man who, by sheer determination, turned a loss-making business into a profitable one within a year — a perfect illustration of this proverb.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Easy come, easy go" — what is gained without effort is lost just as easily; the opposite idea of hard-won success.

• Option 2 "Throw up" — to vomit, or to abandon/give up a job; it suggests failure, not achievement.

• Option 4 "Still waters run deep" — a quiet person may have a deep, thoughtful nature; it describes personality, not effort.

NOTE

• Similar proverbs of determination: "Fortune favours the brave", "No pain, no gain", "Rome was not built in a day", "A determined mind conquers all".

question:
Parts of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains a misspelt word.

Obesity is rapidly becoming the leading cause of prevantable deaths in the United States.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. prevantable.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Prevantable" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "preventable" — from the verb "prevent" + the suffix "-able". It means able to be stopped from happening. (रोके जाने योग्य)

◦ Correct: Obesity is rapidly becoming the leading cause of preventable deaths in the United States.

• Spelling key: PRE + VENT + ABLE (the base verb "prevent" keeps its "e", not "a").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "Obesity" (the condition of being grossly overweight), "rapidly" (quickly) and "leading" (most important/foremost) are all spelt correctly.

NOTE

• Words built the same way: prevent → preventable/preventive, avoid → avoidable, manage → manageable, notice → noticeable. Keep the base word intact before adding "-able" wherever the base is a complete word.

question:
Identify and correct the INCORRECTLY spelt word in the given sentence.

Sliding each bead from one side to the other, the student used the abacus to count out the nember of days in a week.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. number.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The incorrectly spelt word in the sentence is "nember"; its correct spelling is "number", which means a quantity or figure. (संख्या)

◦ Correct: ... the student used the abacus to count out the number of days in a week.

• The question asks you to pick the correct form of the misspelt word, so the answer is the properly spelt "number".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "beed" is wrong — the sentence already has the correct spelling "bead" (a small ball with a hole for threading).

• Option 3 "Slaiding" is wrong — the correct form is "Sliding", which is already used correctly.

• Option 4 "abacuss" is wrong — the correct spelling is "abacus" (a frame with sliding beads used for counting); its plural is abacuses/abaci.

NOTE

• Only ONE word in such sentences is misspelt. Read every word, compare it with the options and choose the option that gives the correct spelling of the faulty word — here, "nember" → "number".

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No improvement required’.

Very early in the morning, at the beginning of January, Opu was lying in bed waiting for the sun having rose.
option_2: waited for the sun having rose
option_4: waiting for the sun to rise
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. waiting for the sun to rise.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The structure "wait for + object + to + V1 (infinitive)" is the correct pattern for expressing what one is waiting to happen. Hence "waiting for the sun to rise".

◦ Correct: Very early in the morning, at the beginning of January, Opu was lying in bed waiting for the sun to rise.

• The main clause already has "was lying" (past continuous); the participle "waiting" correctly runs parallel with it, showing two simultaneous actions.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "waited for the sun rising" wrongly changes "waiting" to the finite verb "waited" after "was lying", producing an ungrammatical string.

• Option 2 "waited for the sun having rose" repeats the same faulty perfect participle; besides, "having rose" is doubly wrong — the past participle of "rise" is "risen" (rise – rose – risen).

• Option 3 "No improvement required" is wrong because the original "waiting for the sun having rose" is clearly ungrammatical.

NOTE

• Verb forms: rise – rose – risen (intransitive, no object) and raise – raised – raised (transitive, takes an object). Pattern to remember: wait for someone/something to do something.

question: Choose the sentence that contains an error.
option_1: I love the taste of fresh strawberries in the summer.
option_2: She is the winner of the Nobel Peace Prize.
option_3: He is chef who specialises in Italian cuisine.
option_4: The Earth revolves around the Sun.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. He is chef who specialises in Italian cuisine.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A singular countable noun ("chef") must be preceded by an article. Since the chef is being introduced for the first time, the indefinite article "a" is required.

◦ Correct: He is a chef who specialises in Italian cuisine.

• "Chef" begins with a consonant sound /ʃ/, so the article used is "a", not "an".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is correct — "the taste of fresh strawberries" and "in the summer" are both acceptable usages.

• Option 2 is correct — "the winner of the Nobel Peace Prize" rightly uses "the" with a unique/definite noun and with the name of a prize.

• Option 4 is correct — "The Earth revolves around the Sun" is a universal truth, correctly expressed in the simple present tense, with "the" before unique objects (Earth, Sun).

NOTE

• Article rules: use a/an with a singular countable noun mentioned for the first time; use the for something already specified, unique (the Sun, the Earth) or superlative/ordinal (the best, the first).

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No improvement required’.

Newton, after seeing the apple falling from a tree, began to wonder whether if it moved towards the earth and not upwards towards the sky.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. began to wonder why.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Whether if" is wrong because "whether" and "if" are two conjunctions with the same function and can never be used together — that is redundancy.

• The sentence explains the reason/cause of the apple's motion ("it moved towards the earth and not upwards"), so the correct question word is "why".

◦ Correct: Newton, after seeing the apple falling from a tree, began to wonder why it moved towards the earth and not upwards towards the sky.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "No improvement required" is wrong because "whether if" is ungrammatical.

• Option 2 "began to wondering if" — after "to" (infinitive marker) the base form (V1) "wonder" is needed, not "wondering".

• Option 3 "began his wondering how" is awkward and "how" would ask about the manner, which the sentence does not discuss.

NOTE

• Use "whether" (not "if") before an infinitive, after a preposition and with "or not": He asked whether to stay or not. Never write "whether if" or "if whether".

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined word in the following sentence.

They serve stuffed garlic bread and molten chocolate in the birthday party of their son, Parth, last week.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. served.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The time expression "last week" refers to a finished action in the past, so the verb must be in the simple past tense — "served" (V2).

◦ Correct: They served stuffed garlic bread and molten chocolate in the birthday party of their son, Parth, last week.

• Rule: adverbials such as yesterday, last week/month/year, ago, in 2019 always take the simple past, never the present or present continuous.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "serves" is simple present (and also singular, whereas the subject "They" is plural) — doubly wrong.

• Option 3 "are serving" is present continuous, which cannot go with "last week".

• Option 4 "be served" is an incomplete passive form with no auxiliary and no agreement with "They".

NOTE

• Tense–time markers: simple past — yesterday, last night, in 2010, ago; present perfect — already, just, yet, since, for; simple present — always, usually, every day.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Barbed
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Spiteful.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Barbed" literally means having sharp points or barbs (as in barbed wire); figuratively, when used of a remark or comment, it means deliberately hurtful, cutting or sarcastic. Its closest synonym here is "spiteful" (full of malice, intending to hurt). (चुभने वाला / द्वेषपूर्ण)

◦ Example: She made a barbed/spiteful comment about his failure.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Passive" (accepting without resistance) is unrelated to sharpness or malice.

• Options 2 "Kind" and 3 "Gentle" are antonyms — they describe warmth and mildness, the opposite of a barbed remark.

NOTE

• Synonyms of barbed: spiteful, cutting, caustic, acerbic, scathing, venomous, sarcastic. Antonyms: kind, gentle, complimentary, soothing. Note the common collocations: barbed wire, a barbed remark.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined segment in the given sentence.

I can't believe you let the cat out of the bag about my surprise party!
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Reveal a secret.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "let the cat out of the bag" means to reveal a secret carelessly or by mistake. (राज़ खोल देना / भेद खोलना)

◦ The sentence is about a surprise party — a secret that has been given away, so the meaning fits perfectly.

• Origin: in old markets a piglet was sold in a sack; a dishonest trader might substitute a cat, and opening the bag exposed the trick.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Ask a question" and Option 4 "Make a joke" have no link with the idiom.

• Option 3 "Keep a secret" is the exact opposite of the idiom's meaning.

NOTE

• Idioms with a similar sense: "spill the beans" (reveal a secret), "blow the whistle" (expose wrongdoing), "give the game away". Opposite: "keep something under wraps", "keep mum".

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

Endless period of time
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Eternity.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Eternity" means time without end; an infinite or endless period of time. (अनंत काल)

◦ Example: To the anxious mother, the ten minutes of waiting felt like an eternity.

• The related adjective is "eternal" (lasting forever) — e.g., eternal life, eternal truth.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Longevity" — long life / long duration of life, but it is finite, not endless.

• Option 3 "Impurity" — the state of being unclean or adulterated.

• Option 4 "Frailty" — weakness of body or character.

NOTE

• Related one-word substitutes: perpetual/everlasting (lasting forever), ephemeral/transient (lasting a very short time), contemporary (belonging to the same time), posthumous (occurring after one's death).

question:
Parts of the given sentence have been underlined. One of them contains an error. The underlined parts are given as options with some changes. Select the option that correctly rectifies the error.

Sohan is the older brother of my best friend.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. elder.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• For members of the same family (brother, sister, son, daughter), the correct comparative adjective placed before the noun is "elder", not "older".

◦ Correct: Sohan is the elder brother of my best friend.

• "Elder/eldest" is used attributively within a family (my elder brother, the eldest son); "older/oldest" is used for people or things in general and always with "than" (He is older than me).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "to my" is wrong — the correct preposition of possession here is "of my best friend".

• Option 2 "an" is wrong — the noun phrase is a definite, specific one, so "the elder brother" is required; also "an" cannot precede the consonant sound of "elder brother" in this structure.

• Option 4 "good" is wrong — the superlative "best friend" is the standard idiomatic expression.

NOTE

• Remember: elder – eldest (family, before the noun, no "than") vs older – oldest (general use, can take "than"). Similar pairs: farther/further, later/latter, nearest/next.

question:
Parts of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

We think of the past history of the world as fixed but of the future as undecided and open to a wealth off possibilities.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. wealth off.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The error is the word "off", which should be the preposition "of". The expression is "a wealth of possibilities", meaning a large amount/an abundance of possibilities.

◦ Correct: ... open to a wealth of possibilities.

• "Of" is a preposition showing belonging/quantity; "off" means away from / not on (He fell off the ladder).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "of the past" is correct — "the past history of the world" is an acceptable noun phrase.

• "as fixed" and "as undecided" are correct — the structure "think of X as Y" (to regard X as Y) is properly maintained in both parallel parts.

NOTE

• Commonly confused pairs: of / off, quite / quiet, loose / lose, advice / advise, effect / affect. Useful collocations with "a wealth of": a wealth of experience, a wealth of information, a wealth of talent.

question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

My teacher told me that / all that / glitters was not gold.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. glitters was not gold.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "All that glitters is not gold" is a universal truth / proverb. When a reported clause states a universal truth or a proverb, the tense is NOT changed even after a past reporting verb ("told"). Hence "was" must remain "is".

◦ Correct: My teacher told me that all that glitters is not gold.

• Rule: Reported speech — a fact that is always true, a habitual truth or a proverb keeps the present tense.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "My teacher told me that" is correct — "tell" takes an indirect object ("told me") and is properly followed by the conjunction "that".

• "all that" is correct — "all that glitters" means "everything that shines".

• Since a clear error exists, Option 4 "No error" cannot be chosen.

NOTE

• Other cases where the tense does NOT back-shift in indirect speech: universal truths (The sun rises in the east), habitual facts, mathematical/scientific facts, and historical facts. The proverb means: not everything that looks attractive is truly valuable.

question:
Parts of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

When I bought the book, I thought it will be interesting.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. will.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sequence of tenses rule states that when the principal clause is in the past tense ("I thought"), the subordinate clause must also take a past form. So the future auxiliary "will" must become "would".

◦ Correct: When I bought the book, I thought it would be interesting.

• "would" here is the past form of "will" and expresses "future in the past".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "When" is correct — it properly introduces the time clause.

• "bought" is correct — the simple past (V2) of "buy" (buy – bought – bought) suits the completed past action.

• "thought" is correct — the simple past (V2) of "think" (think – thought – thought), which fixes the past time frame.

NOTE

• Back-shifting of modals after a past main verb: will → would, shall → should, can → could, may → might, must → had to. Exception: universal truths keep the present tense.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Education should be free to all because it is a (1)__ human right. It is essential for the (2)___ of a fully functioning society and for the advancement of humanity. While some argue that education should not be free because it has value or that free education would be a (3)__ on taxpayers, the reality is that education is a public good that (4)__ everyone in society. Not only does education provide individuals with the skills and knowledge they need to participate in the workforce, but it also improves social cohesion and creates more (5)__ citizens.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. fundamental.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Fundamental" means basic, essential and forming the foundation of something. The standard, fixed collocation used in law and in human-rights discourse is "a fundamental human right". (मौलिक अधिकार)

◦ Correct: Education should be free to all because it is a fundamental human right.

• The very next sentence begins "It is essential for the ...", which confirms that the writer is stressing how basic and indispensable education is.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "lovely" (beautiful, pleasant) and Option 4 "joyful" (full of joy) are emotional/aesthetic words that do not describe a right.

• Option 2 "precious" (valuable) sounds positive but is not used with "human right"; moreover, the passage later argues against treating education merely as something of commercial "value".

NOTE

• In the Indian Constitution, Article 21A makes free and compulsory education for children aged 6–14 years a Fundamental Right (86th Amendment, 2002), implemented through the RTE Act, 2009.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Education should be free to all because it is a (1)__ human right. It is essential for the (2)___ of a fully functioning society and for the advancement of humanity. While some argue that education should not be free because it has value or that free education would be a (3)__ on taxpayers, the reality is that education is a public good that (4)__ everyone in society. Not only does education provide individuals with the skills and knowledge they need to participate in the workforce, but it also improves social cohesion and creates more (5)__ citizens.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. development.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Development" means the process of growing, building up or advancing. The blank needs a noun that goes with "of a fully functioning society" and runs parallel with "the advancement of humanity" in the same sentence. (विकास)

◦ Correct: It is essential for the development of a fully functioning society and for the advancement of humanity.

• The parallel structure "for the development of ... and for the advancement of ..." makes the answer certain.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "celebration" (festivity) and Option 3 "enthusiasm" (eagerness) do not combine logically with "of a fully functioning society".

• Option 4 "distribution" (the act of sharing out) would suggest handing out a society, which is meaningless here.

NOTE

• Look for parallel words in the same sentence while solving cloze tests. Here "advancement" is the strongest clue pointing to its near-synonym "development".

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Education should be free to all because it is a (1)__ human right. It is essential for the (2)___ of a fully functioning society and for the advancement of humanity. While some argue that education should not be free because it has value or that free education would be a (3)__ on taxpayers, the reality is that education is a public good that (4)__ everyone in society. Not only does education provide individuals with the skills and knowledge they need to participate in the workforce, but it also improves social cohesion and creates more (5)__ citizens.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. burden.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Burden" means a heavy load or an onerous responsibility. The clause begins with "While some argue that education should not be free", so the blank must carry a negative idea — the objection that free education places a financial load on taxpayers. (बोझ)

◦ Correct: ... free education would be a burden on taxpayers ...

• The preposition "on" is the clinching clue: the fixed collocation is "a burden on (someone)".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 4 "blessing" is positive and would contradict the contrastive word "While" that opens the clause.

• Option 1 "focus" (centre of attention) and Option 2 "contentment" (satisfaction) do not collocate with "on taxpayers" in this sense.

NOTE

• Contrast markers such as while, although, though, whereas, however, but signal that the two halves of the sentence carry opposite ideas — a vital clue in cloze passages. Collocations: a burden on/upon, bear a burden, ease the burden.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Education should be free to all because it is a (1)__ human right. It is essential for the (2)___ of a fully functioning society and for the advancement of humanity. While some argue that education should not be free because it has value or that free education would be a (3)__ on taxpayers, the reality is that education is a public good that (4)__ everyone in society. Not only does education provide individuals with the skills and knowledge they need to participate in the workforce, but it also improves social cohesion and creates more (5)__ citizens.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. benefits.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Benefits" (verb) means does good to; is advantageous to. The writer is now stating his own view — "the reality is that" — namely that education is a public good that does good to everyone in society. (लाभ पहुँचाता है)

◦ Correct: ... the reality is that education is a public good that benefits everyone in society.

• The relative pronoun "that" stands for the singular noun "a public good", so the verb takes "-s": benefits.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 3 "burdens" would repeat the objection the writer is refuting, contradicting the phrase "the reality is that".

• Option 2 "emphasises" (stresses) does not fit "everyone in society" as an object.

• Option 1 "sections" is a noun, but the slot after the relative pronoun "that" requires a verb.

NOTE

• A public good in economics is non-rival and non-excludable — one person's use does not reduce its availability to others, and no one can be kept from using it (e.g., street lighting, national defence, basic education).

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Education should be free to all because it is a (1)__ human right. It is essential for the (2)___ of a fully functioning society and for the advancement of humanity. While some argue that education should not be free because it has value or that free education would be a (3)__ on taxpayers, the reality is that education is a public good that (4)__ everyone in society. Not only does education provide individuals with the skills and knowledge they need to participate in the workforce, but it also improves social cohesion and creates more (5)__ citizens.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. productive.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Productive" means achieving or producing a great deal; useful and effective. The sentence says education gives people "the skills and knowledge they need to participate in the workforce" — therefore it creates more productive citizens. (उत्पादक / फलदायी)

◦ Correct: ... it also improves social cohesion and creates more productive citizens.

• The comparative marker "more" also requires an adjective, and "productive" is the only one that logically follows from workforce participation.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "easy going" (relaxed, tolerant) is a personality trait unconnected with education's social value.

• Option 2 "apprehensive" (anxious, fearful) is negative and contradicts the positive tone.

• Option 4 "authentic" (genuine) does not collocate meaningfully with "citizens" here.

NOTE

• Note the structure at the end of the passage: "Not only does education provide ..., but it also improves ..." — after "Not only" at the beginning of a clause, the sentence takes inversion (auxiliary before the subject).

question: How many countries participated in the FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 16.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A total of 16 countries (teams) participated in the FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup 2022, which was hosted by India from 11 to 30 October 2022. (फीफा अंडर-17 महिला विश्व कप 2022 — 16 टीमें)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The 2022 edition was the seventh FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup and the matches were played in Bhubaneswar (Odisha), Margao (Goa) and Navi Mumbai (Maharashtra).

• Spain won the title by defeating Colombia 1–0 in the final at Navi Mumbai.

• India took part as the host nation — its first appearance in a FIFA World Cup event of any kind.

NOTE

• India had earlier been chosen to host the FIFA U-17 Men's World Cup in 2017. The world governing body of football is FIFA (Fédération Internationale de Football Association), founded in 1904, with headquarters in Zurich, Switzerland.

question: ‘Wings of Fire’ is the autobiography of a former president of India. Who is he?
solution_text:
The correct answer is APJ Abdul Kalam.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Wings of Fire" (1999) is the autobiography of Dr. A. P. J. Abdul Kalam, the 11th President of India (2002–2007). It was co-authored with Arun Tiwari. (विंग्स ऑफ फायर — डॉ. ए.पी.जे. अब्दुल कलाम)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Dr. Kalam is known as the "Missile Man of India" for his work on the Agni and Prithvi missiles and India's SLV-III launch vehicle; he also played a key role in the Pokhran-II nuclear tests (1998).

• He received the Bharat Ratna in 1997, and his birthday, 15 October, is observed as World Students' Day.

• His other books include India 2020, Ignited Minds, My Journey, Turning Points and The Luminous Sparks.

NOTE

• Books by other leaders: Shankar Dayal Sharma — Constitution, Parliament and Society; V. V. Giri — My Life and Times, Jobs for Our Millions; Zakir Hussain was the third President of India and the first Muslim to hold the office.

question: In which of the following states is the Statue of Unity situated?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gujarat.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Statue of Unity, the statue of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, is situated at Kevadiya in the Narmada district of Gujarat, facing the Sardar Sarovar Dam on the Narmada river. (स्टैच्यू ऑफ यूनिटी — गुजरात)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• At 182 metres (597 feet), it is the tallest statue in the world; it was unveiled on 31 October 2018 on Patel's 143rd birth anniversary by Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

• It was designed by the sculptor Ram V. Sutar.

• Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel was India's first Deputy Prime Minister and first Home Minister, called the "Iron Man of India" for integrating over 560 princely states.

NOTE

• 31 October is observed as Rashtriya Ekta Diwas (National Unity Day) in memory of Sardar Patel. Other famous Indian statues: the Statue of Equality (Ramanuja, Hyderabad) and the Statue of Belief (Shiva, Nathdwara, Rajasthan).

question: When was the Defence of India Act enacted?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1915.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Defence of India Act was enacted in 1915 by the British colonial government during the First World War. It was an emergency criminal law that gave the government sweeping powers of preventive detention, trial without appeal by special tribunals and restriction of movement, speech and writing. (भारत रक्षा अधिनियम — 1915)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• It was aimed chiefly at suppressing the Ghadar Movement and other revolutionary activity in Punjab and Bengal.

• Many revolutionaries, including those of the Ghadar Party and the Lahore Conspiracy Case, were tried under this Act.

• Its wartime provisions were later carried into peacetime through the Rowlatt Act of 1919, based on the recommendations of the Sedition (Rowlatt) Committee, which provoked nationwide protest and led to the Jallianwala Bagh massacre (13 April 1919).

NOTE

• Repressive colonial laws to remember: Vernacular Press Act (1878), Arms Act (1878), Indian Press Act (1910), Defence of India Act (1915) and the Rowlatt Act (1919) — described by Gandhiji as "no dalil, no vakil, no appeal".

question: Which festival brings out the fusion rich culture of Chhattisgarh and Odisha?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bastar Goncha.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Bastar Goncha" is the festival celebrated in the Bastar region of Chhattisgarh that reflects the fusion of the cultures of Chhattisgarh and Odisha. It is closely linked to the Rath Yatra tradition of Lord Jagannath of Puri (Odisha), which the rulers of Bastar brought to their kingdom. (बस्तर गोंचा — छत्तीसगढ़ और ओडिशा की मिश्रित संस्कृति)

• During the festival devotees fire a local fruit called "tupki" (a bamboo pop-gun with the malkangani fruit) as a mark of celebration and salute to the deity.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Bastar Dussehra, celebrated for about 75 days, is one of the longest festivals in the world and is also from the Bastar region of Chhattisgarh.

• Option 3 "Shoolini fair" is celebrated at Solan in Himachal Pradesh in honour of goddess Shoolini Devi.

• Option 4 "Madhavpur fair/mela" is held at Madhavpur (Ghed) in Gujarat, marking the wedding of Lord Krishna and Rukmini, and celebrates the cultural link between Gujarat and the North-East.

NOTE

• Chhattisgarh was carved out of Madhya Pradesh on 1 November 2000; its capital is Raipur. Its other well-known festivals/dances include Bastar Dussehra, Madai, Pandwani, Raut Nacha and Panthi.

question: Which flag of the Indian National Congress was adopted in 1931?
option_1: A two colour flag with charkha made by cloth
option_2: A tricolour flag made by Khadi with a Charkha symbol
option_3: One colour flag with charkha symbol
option_4: A blue colour flag made by cloth
solution_text:
The correct answer is A tricolour flag made by Khadi with a Charkha symbol.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In 1931, the Karachi session of the Indian National Congress formally adopted a tricolour flag made of khadi, with horizontal bands of saffron, white and green and a charkha (spinning wheel) in the centre of the white band. (1931 — खादी का तिरंगा ध्वज, चरखे के साथ)

• A special Flag Committee (1931) recommended this design, and the charkha stood for self-reliance, dignity of labour and the swadeshi movement.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The earlier Swaraj flag of 1921, designed by Pingali Venkayya and modified on Gandhiji's suggestion, had red and green bands (later with a white band added) with a charkha.

• On 22 July 1947, the Constituent Assembly adopted the present National Flag, in which the charkha was replaced by the Ashoka Chakra (a 24-spoked wheel taken from the Sarnath Lion Capital).

NOTE

• Meaning of the colours of the national flag: saffron — courage and sacrifice; white — truth and peace; green — faith, fertility and prosperity. The ratio of the flag is 3:2, and the flag code is governed by the Flag Code of India, 2002.

question: Among the following pairs, which ones denote two scalar quantities?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Distance and Speed.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A scalar quantity has only magnitude and no direction, whereas a vector quantity has both magnitude and direction.

• Both "distance" (the total path length covered) and "speed" (distance covered per unit time) have only magnitude, so they are scalars. (अदिश राशियाँ — दूरी और चाल)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 — momentum (mass × velocity) and angular velocity are both vectors.

• Option 3 — linear momentum and acceleration are both vectors.

• Option 4 — electric field and force are both vectors.

• Note the contrasting pairs: distance (scalar) – displacement (vector) and speed (scalar) – velocity (vector).

NOTE

• Common scalars: mass, time, distance, speed, work, energy, power, temperature, density, volume, electric charge, potential.

• Common vectors: displacement, velocity, acceleration, force, momentum, torque, weight, electric field, magnetic field.

question: Which of the following music directors won the Oscar award in the year 2009?
solution_text:
The correct answer is AR Rahman.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The music director A. R. Rahman won two Academy Awards (Oscars) in 2009 for the film "Slumdog Millionaire" — for Best Original Score and for Best Original Song ("Jai Ho", the lyrics being by Gulzar). (ए. आर. रहमान — ऑस्कर 2009)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• In the same year he also won two Grammy Awards and a Golden Globe for the same film. Resul Pookutty won the Oscar for Best Sound Mixing for Slumdog Millionaire as well.

• A. R. Rahman (born A. S. Dileep Kumar) is called the "Mozart of Madras"; he has received the Padma Shri (2000), the Padma Bhushan (2010) and several National Film Awards.

NOTE

• Other Indian Oscar winners: Bhanu Athaiya (Costume Design, Gandhi, 1983), Satyajit Ray (Honorary Award, 1992), Guneet Monga & Kartiki Gonsalves (The Elephant Whisperers, 2023) and M. M. Keeravani & Chandrabose ("Naatu Naatu" from RRR, 2023).

question: Which of the following vitamins prevents major birth defects of the brain and spine of a newborn baby?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Folic acid.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Folic acid" (Vitamin B9, also called folate) prevents major birth defects of the brain and spine of a newborn baby, known as neural tube defects — for example, spina bifida and anencephaly. Pregnant women are therefore advised to take folic acid supplements. (फोलिक एसिड — विटामिन B9)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Folic acid is also essential for the formation of red blood cells and DNA synthesis; its deficiency causes megaloblastic anaemia.

• Sources: green leafy vegetables, citrus fruits, beans, liver and fortified cereals.

• Option 1 Vitamin E (tocopherol) — an antioxidant; deficiency can cause infertility.

• Option 2 Vitamin A (retinol) — needed for vision; deficiency causes night blindness and xerophthalmia.

• Option 3 Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) — deficiency causes scurvy.

NOTE

• Water-soluble vitamins: B-complex and C; fat-soluble vitamins: A, D, E, K. Vitamin B9 (folic acid) and B12 (cyanocobalamin) work together in red blood cell formation.

question: In India, the National Sports Day is celebrated on which date?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 29th August.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• National Sports Day is celebrated in India on 29 August every year, marking the birth anniversary of the hockey legend Major Dhyan Chand (born 29 August 1905). (राष्ट्रीय खेल दिवस — 29 अगस्त)

• On this day the President of India confers the national sports honours at Rashtrapati Bhavan.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Major Dhyan Chand, known as "The Wizard/Magician of Hockey", won Olympic gold medals for India in 1928 (Amsterdam), 1932 (Los Angeles) and 1936 (Berlin). He was awarded the Padma Bhushan in 1956.

• India's highest sporting honour, earlier the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna, was renamed the "Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award" in 2021.

• The Dhyan Chand Award is given for lifetime achievement in sports.

NOTE

• Other important days: 14 November — Children's Day (Nehru's birthday); 1 September — National Nutrition Week begins; 5 September — Teachers' Day (Dr. S. Radhakrishnan); 6 April — International Day of Sport for Development and Peace.

question: Who among the following was the founding member of Sri Sai Nataraja Academy of Kuchipudi that offers training and higher studies in Kuchipudi?
solution_text:
The correct answer is P Ramadevi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• P. Ramadevi, a distinguished exponent and teacher of Kuchipudi, was the founding member of the Sri Sai Nataraja Academy of Kuchipudi, an institution that provides training and higher studies in the Kuchipudi dance form. (पी. रमादेवी — श्री साईं नटराज कुचिपुड़ी अकादमी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Kuchipudi is the classical dance–drama of Andhra Pradesh, named after the village of Kuchipudi (Kuchelapuram) in the Krishna district. It was systematised in the 17th century by Siddhendra Yogi.

• Its best-known items are the "Tarangam" (dancing on the rim of a brass plate, often balancing a pot of water on the head) and the Bhamakalapam.

• Yamini Krishnamurthy (Option 3) was a celebrated Bharatanatyam and Kuchipudi dancer and a Padma Vibhushan awardee, but she is associated with her own dance school, not this academy.

NOTE

• The eight classical dance forms of India: Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (North India), Kathakali and Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur) and Sattriya (Assam).

question: Which of the following playback singers of India received the Padma Shri in 2009 and Padma Bhushan in 2016?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Udit Narayan Jha.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The playback singer Udit Narayan Jha received the Padma Shri in 2009 and the Padma Bhushan in 2016 for his contribution to Indian music. (उदित नारायण झा — पद्म श्री 2009, पद्म भूषण 2016)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Udit Narayan has won three National Film Awards and several Filmfare Awards; he has sung in more than 35 languages, with famous songs from Qayamat Se Qayamat Tak, Dil To Pagal Hai, Lagaan and Jodhaa Akbar.

• Kumar Sanu (Option 3) received the Padma Shri in 2009 as well, but not the Padma Bhushan in 2016.

• Sonu Nigam (Option 1) received the Padma Shri in 2022.

NOTE

• Order of civilian awards (highest to lowest): Bharat Ratna → Padma Vibhushan → Padma Bhushan → Padma Shri. They are announced on Republic Day (26 January) and were instituted in 1954.

question: When the ‘trans-boundary economic activities’ of an economy and depreciation are included into account, the aggregate measure is known as ____________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is GNP.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "GNP (Gross National Product)" is the aggregate measure that takes the trans-boundary (cross-border) economic activities of an economy into account and is still a "gross" figure, i.e., depreciation is included in (not deducted from) it. (सकल राष्ट्रीय उत्पाद)

◦ GNP = GDP + Net Factor Income from Abroad (NFIA), where NFIA is the income earned by residents abroad minus the income earned by foreigners within the country — exactly the "trans-boundary" component.

◦ The word "Gross" means that depreciation (consumption of fixed capital) has not been subtracted.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 4 "GDP (Gross Domestic Product)" counts only production within the domestic territory, so it leaves out trans-boundary income altogether.

• Option 2 "NNP (Net National Product)" = GNP – Depreciation; here depreciation has been removed, so it is a "net", not a "gross", measure.

• Option 3 "PCI (Per Capita Income)" = National Income ÷ Total Population; it is an average, not an aggregate.

NOTE

• Key national-income identities: GNP = GDP + NFIA; NNP = GNP − Depreciation; National Income (NNP at factor cost) = NNP at market price − Indirect taxes + Subsidies. In India these estimates are prepared by the NSO (National Statistical Office) under MoSPI.

question: Tamil Nadu’s _____________ marked a national record in men’s long jump in the second AFI National Jumps Competition in March 2023.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jeswin Aldrin.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Jeswin Aldrin of Tamil Nadu set a national record in the men's long jump with a leap of 8.42 m at the second Indian Open Jumps (AFI National Jumps) Competition held in March 2023 at Bellary, Karnataka. (जेसविन एल्ड्रिन — 8.42 मीटर राष्ट्रीय रिकॉर्ड)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• He broke the earlier national record of 8.36 m set by Murali Sreeshankar (Option 3), the Kerala long-jumper who won silver at the 2022 Commonwealth Games.

• Suresh Babu (Option 1) was an earlier Indian long-jump record holder and an Asian Games bronze medallist (1978).

• Athletics in India is governed by the Athletics Federation of India (AFI), founded in 1946, with headquarters in New Delhi.

NOTE

• Notable Indian athletics performances: Neeraj Chopra — Olympic gold in javelin throw (Tokyo 2020); Avinash Sable — national record in the 3000 m steeplechase; Anju Bobby George — bronze in long jump at the 2003 World Championships, the first Indian to win a World Championship medal.

question: On the arrival of the spring season, the _____________ village sways to the melodious singing of ‘Bagurumba’.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bodo.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Bagurumba" is the traditional folk dance and song of the Bodo tribe of Assam, performed chiefly by women in the spring season (during the Bwisagu festival). Hence it is the Bodo village that comes alive with the melodious singing of Bagurumba. (बागुरुम्बा — असम की बोडो जनजाति)

• Because the graceful movements imitate the fluttering of butterflies and birds, it is popularly called the "butterfly dance".

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Bodos are the largest plains tribe of Assam; the Bodoland Territorial Region (BTR) was formed for them, and the Bodo language is in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution.

• Option 2 Khasi — a tribe of Meghalaya, famous for the Shad Suk Mynsiem and Nongkrem dances.

• Option 3 Garo — also of Meghalaya, known for the Wangala ("hundred drums") harvest festival.

• Option 4 Karbi — a tribe of Assam's Karbi Anglong, known for the Chomangkan festival.

NOTE

• Folk dances of Assam: Bihu (the state's best-known dance, of the Bihu festival), Bagurumba (Bodo), Jhumur (tea-tribe), Ojapali and Sattriya (which is a classical form).

question: Which mountain range from the following is associated with Rajasthan state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Aravalli Range.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Aravalli Range" is the mountain range associated with Rajasthan. It runs roughly north-east to south-west for about 800 km, from Delhi through Haryana and Rajasthan up to Gujarat (Palanpur). (अरावली पर्वतमाला — राजस्थान)

• Its highest peak is Guru Shikhar (1,722 m) on Mount Abu, the only hill station of Rajasthan.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Aravallis are the oldest fold mountains in India (of the Precambrian era) and are now much eroded; they act as a barrier against the eastward spread of the Thar Desert.

• Option 1 Satpura Range — lies mainly in Madhya Pradesh/Maharashtra; highest peak Dhupgarh (Pachmarhi).

• Option 2 Sahyadri Range — another name for the Western Ghats, along the western coast (Maharashtra, Goa, Karnataka, Kerala); highest peak Anamudi (Kerala).

• Option 4 Vindhya Range — runs across central India and traditionally separates North India from the Deccan.

NOTE

• The Aravallis are the source of rivers such as the Banas, Luni and Sabarmati. Rajasthan is India's largest state by area, with its capital at Jaipur.

question: According to the National Multidimensional Poverty Index 2021, which state has the lowest percentage of population being multidimensionally poor?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kerala.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• According to the National Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) 2021, released by NITI Aayog, Kerala had the lowest percentage of population that is multidimensionally poor (about 0.71%) among the states. (राष्ट्रीय बहुआयामी गरीबी सूचकांक 2021 — केरल सबसे कम गरीब)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Kerala was followed by Puducherry, Lakshadweep, Goa and Sikkim among the least poor; Bihar had the highest share of multidimensionally poor, followed by Jharkhand, Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh.

• India's national MPI is based on the Alkire–Foster methodology and uses 12 indicators across three equally weighted dimensions — Health, Education and Standard of Living.

• The data source was the National Family Health Survey-4 (2015–16) for the baseline report.

NOTE

• The global MPI is published jointly by the UNDP and the Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI). India's index adds two extra indicators — maternal health and bank accounts — to the global set of ten.

question: Which of the following represents disposable income?
option_1: The income earned by individuals and households after taxes and other deductions
option_2: The total income earned by businesses and corporations in an economy
option_3: The income earned by individuals through their own business or self-employment
option_4: The total income earned by individuals and households before taxes and other deductions
solution_text:
The correct answer is The income earned by individuals and households after taxes and other deductions.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Disposable income" is the income that is actually available to individuals and households for spending and saving after direct taxes and other compulsory deductions have been paid. (प्रयोज्य आय / व्ययनीय आय)

◦ Formula: Personal Disposable Income = Personal Income − Direct (personal) taxes − Miscellaneous receipts of the government.

◦ It is further divided into consumption and savings: Disposable Income = Consumption + Savings.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 4 describes gross/personal income before tax, not disposable income.

• Option 2 describes corporate/business income, which is a different aggregate.

• Option 3 describes income from self-employment (mixed income), only one component of personal income.

NOTE

• Related concept: discretionary income = disposable income minus essential spending on food, rent and utilities. In macroeconomics, disposable income is the key determinant of the consumption function in the Keynesian model.

question: Which of the following states receives rainfall during the winter season?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tamil Nadu.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Tamil Nadu (especially the Coromandel Coast) receives most of its rainfall in the winter season (October–December) from the retreating or North-East Monsoon. (तमिलनाडु — शीतकालीन/लौटता मानसून वर्षा)

• As the north-east winds blow from land to sea, they pick up moisture over the Bay of Bengal and shed it on the eastern coast of Tamil Nadu, which lies on the leeward side of the Western Ghats during the south-west monsoon and therefore stays comparatively dry from June to September.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Jharkhand, Maharashtra and Rajasthan receive their rain mainly from the South-West Monsoon (June–September).

• North-western India (Punjab, Haryana, western UP) gets some light winter rain from Western Disturbances — extra-tropical storms originating over the Mediterranean Sea — which are very useful for the rabi crop, especially wheat.

NOTE

• India's four seasons as classified by the IMD: Winter (Dec–Feb), Summer/Pre-monsoon (Mar–May), South-West Monsoon (Jun–Sep) and Post-monsoon/Retreating Monsoon (Oct–Dec).

question: Who among the following is the author of the book ‘Revolution 2020’?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chetan Bhagat.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Revolution 2020: Love, Corruption, Ambition" (published in 2011) is a novel written by the Indian author Chetan Bhagat. It is set in Varanasi and deals with the education mafia, corruption and ambition. (रेवोल्यूशन 2020 — चेतन भगत)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Chetan Bhagat's other well-known novels include Five Point Someone, One Night @ the Call Center, The 3 Mistakes of My Life, 2 States, Half Girlfriend, One Indian Girl and The Girl in Room 105.

• Several have been filmed — Five Point Someone as 3 Idiots, The 3 Mistakes of My Life as Kai Po Che! and One Night @ the Call Center as Hello.

• Option 2 Omair Ahmad wrote Jimmy the Terrorist; Option 3 Siddhartha Sarma wrote The Grasshopper's Run; Option 4 Joy Goswami is a noted Bengali poet and Sahitya Akademi awardee.

NOTE

• Chetan Bhagat, an alumnus of IIT Delhi and IIM Ahmedabad, was named by Time magazine among the 100 most influential people in the world (2010).

question: Who was our first Prime Minister?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jawaharlal Nehru.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru was the first Prime Minister of India, holding office from 15 August 1947 until his death on 27 May 1964 — the longest-serving Indian Prime Minister. (पंडित जवाहरलाल नेहरू — प्रथम प्रधानमंत्री)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Nehru delivered the famous "Tryst with Destiny" speech on the midnight of 14–15 August 1947, set up the Planning Commission (1950) and launched the Five Year Plans (from 1951), and was a founder of the Non-Aligned Movement along with the Panchsheel principles.

• His birthday, 14 November, is celebrated as Children's Day (Bal Diwas). He wrote The Discovery of India, Glimpses of World History and An Autobiography.

• Option 1 Dr. Rajendra Prasad was India's first President; Option 4 Gulzarilal Nanda was the first acting Prime Minister (twice, in 1964 and 1966); Option 2 Indira Gandhi was India's first woman Prime Minister (1966).

NOTE

• The Prime Minister is appointed by the President under Article 75 and is the real executive head, while the President is the nominal/constitutional head of the Indian Union.

question: Which state is ranked fourth in India according to the first Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) 2021 report of the NITI Aayog?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Madhya Pradesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• According to the first National Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) report of NITI Aayog (2021), Madhya Pradesh stood fourth among the states with the highest share of multidimensionally poor population (about 36.65%). (एमपीआई 2021 — मध्य प्रदेश चौथे स्थान पर)

• The order of the poorest states was: 1. Bihar (51.91%) → 2. Jharkhand (42.16%) → 3. Uttar Pradesh (37.79%) → 4. Madhya Pradesh (36.65%) → 5. Meghalaya (32.67%).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The report was released in November 2021 and was based on the National Family Health Survey-4 (2015–16).

• The index uses three dimensions — Health, Education and Standard of Living — with 12 indicators: nutrition, child and adolescent mortality, antenatal care, years of schooling, school attendance, cooking fuel, sanitation, drinking water, electricity, housing, assets and bank accounts.

NOTE

• NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India) replaced the Planning Commission on 1 January 2015. Its Chairperson is the Prime Minister, and it functions as a policy think-tank of the Government of India.

question: Which Schedule of the Indian Constitution deals with the division of powers between the Union and the states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 7th.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution deals with the division of legislative powers between the Union and the States. It contains three lists: (सातवीं अनुसूची — संघ और राज्यों के बीच शक्तियों का विभाजन)

◦ Union List — subjects on which only Parliament can legislate (defence, foreign affairs, railways, banking, currency, atomic energy).

◦ State List — subjects for state legislatures (police, public order, public health, agriculture, local government).

◦ Concurrent List — subjects for both (education, forests, marriage, criminal law, bankruptcy).

• It is linked to Article 246 of the Constitution.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 4 Second Schedule — salaries, allowances and emoluments of the President, Governors, Judges, CAG, etc.

• Option 3 Fifth Schedule — administration and control of Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes.

• Option 1 Ninth Schedule — Acts and Regulations (mainly land reform laws) protected from judicial review; added by the First Amendment, 1951.

NOTE

• The Constitution originally had 8 Schedules; there are now 12. In case of a conflict on a Concurrent List subject, the Union law prevails (Article 254). Residuary powers rest with Parliament (Article 248).

question: What is the name of the scheme launched by the Government of India for the financial inclusion of path or street vendors, the anniversary celebration of which was organised from 9 July to 31 July 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is PM SVANidhi Scheme.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "PM SVANidhi" — Pradhan Mantri Street Vendor's AtmaNirbhar Nidhi — is the scheme launched by the Government of India (Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs) on 1 June 2020 for the financial inclusion of street vendors whose livelihood was hit by the COVID-19 lockdown. (पीएम स्वनिधि योजना — पथ विक्रेता)

• Its second anniversary celebration ("SVANidhi Mahotsav") was organised from 9 July to 31 July 2022.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The scheme provides collateral-free working capital loans: a first loan of ₹10,000, then ₹20,000, and then ₹50,000, repayable in instalments.

• It offers a 7% interest subsidy and cashback of up to ₹1,200 a year for digital transactions, to promote digital payments among vendors.

• It is implemented through SIDBI, with Small Finance Banks, MFIs and SHG banks as lending partners.

NOTE

• Related welfare schemes: PM Jan Dhan Yojana (bank accounts for all), PM MUDRA Yojana (micro-enterprise loans), Stand-Up India and PM Awas Yojana (housing). Street vendors' rights are also protected by the Street Vendors (Protection of Livelihood and Regulation of Street Vending) Act, 2014.

question: Renowned _____________ folk dance artist Domar Singh Kunwar, who has dedicated his life to preserving the tradition of the dance for over five decades, was awarded the Padma Shri 2023.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Natya Nacha.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Domar Singh Kunwar of Chhattisgarh is the renowned "Natya Nacha" folk dance artist who devoted more than five decades to preserving this traditional folk dance–theatre form and was honoured with the Padma Shri in 2023 in the field of Art. (डोमार सिंह कुंवर — नाट्य नाचा, पद्म श्री 2023)

• "Nacha" is the traditional folk theatre of Chhattisgarh, performed at night in the open, combining dance, song, humour and satire; men traditionally play the female roles ("Parry").

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Pandwani" is the sung narration of the Mahabharata in Chhattisgarh, made famous by Padma Vibhushan Teejan Bai.

• Option 2 "Raut Nacha" is the dance of the Yadav/cowherd community of Chhattisgarh, performed around Dev Uthni Ekadashi.

• Option 4 "Soowa (Sua) dance" is the parrot dance performed by women of Chhattisgarh around the harvest and Diwali season.

NOTE

• Other well-known folk arts of Chhattisgarh: Panthi (of the Satnami community), Karma, Saila and Bastar Dussehra. The Padma Shri is India's fourth-highest civilian award, announced every year on Republic Day.
